To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
all four biomaterials facilitated new bone formation, osseointegration and defect closure.
the different BCP materials showed comparable osseointegration and bone-to-implat contact values.
the different BCP materials with different surface properties showed comparable results to NBM in terms of new bone formation and implant osseointegration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of the surface topographies of different bone graft materials on the regeneration of alveolar bone defects.
the influence of different bone graft materials on bone formation in alveolar ridge augmentations in a minipigs model.
a novel approach of staged implant placement after bone defect regeneration using different BCP materials.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the different BCP materials showed similar bone formation and osseoconductivity, but the NBM group showed a significantly higher residual graft material.
the different surface topography of the BCP materials does not influence the osseointegration and bone formation in the investigated minipig model.
all four materials showed comparable bone formation and osseo-integration after 12 weeks of healing and 8 weeks implantation, with no statistically significant differences.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the surface topography of BCP materials has an influence on bone regeneration and osseointegrability.
all four biomaterials investigated showed comparable osseointegration and bone formation.
the different BCP materials with their different surface topographies showed comparable bone regeneration and osseointegrated well into the bone, but with different amounts of residual material.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the surface properties of the bone grafting materials did not significantly influence bone formation and osseeointegration.
BCPs are a suitable alternative for NBM in alveolar ridge augmentation procedures.
